''Zeleno-žuti'' (The Green-Yellows) | short name = Istra, IST | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1948}} | ground = [[Stadion Aldo Drosina]] | capacity = 10,000 | owner = Baskonia-Alavés Group | chrtitle = President | chairman = Branko Devide Vincenti | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Javier Cabello]] | league = [[Croatian Football League]] | season = [[2025–26 Croatian Football League|2025–26]] | position = Croatian Football League, 6th of 10 | website = {{URL|https://nkistra.com/}} | pattern_la1 = _istra1819h | pattern_b1 = _istra1819h | pattern_ra1 = _istra1819h | pattern_sh1 = | leftarm1 = ffe100 | body1 = ffe100 | rightarm1 = ffe100 | shorts1 = 0c9e16 | socks1 = ffff00 | pattern_la2 = _istra1819a | pattern_b2 = _istra1819a | pattern_ra2 = _istra1819a | pattern_sh2 = | leftarm2 = 000000 | body2 = 000000 | rightarm2 = 000000 | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 | current = 2026–27 NK Istra 1961 season }} '''Nogometni klub Istra 1961''' ({{langx|en|Istra 1961 Football Club}}), commonly referred to as '''Istra 1961,''' is a [[Football in Croatia|Croatian]] professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Pula]]. They compete in the [[Croatian Football League]] (HNL), the top tier of [[Croatian football league system|Croatian football]]. It is commonly believed that ''Istra 1961'' was founded in 1961 by merging two clubs from Pula, NK Uljanik and NK Pula, forming [[NK Istra Pula|NK Istra]]. However, NK Istra is not the same club as NK Istra 1961. NK Istra 1961, then named NK Uljanik, was founded in 1964. NK Istra were competing in Prva HNL since the [[1992 Croatian First Football League|first season]], but were relegated in the [[1996–97 Croatian First Football League|1996–97]] season to [[Croatian Second Football League|Druga HNL]]. They were promoted back to Prva HNL in the [[1998–99 Croatian Second Football League|1998–99]] season, but they were relegated again in the next season, never coming back to Prva HNL. Meanwhile, NK Uljanik was in the shadow of NK Istra, but they were promoted to Prva HNL in the [[2003–04 Croatian Second Football League|2003–04]] season and are the best club in Pula since then. NK Istra, now under the name NK Istra Pula, is competing in [[First County Football League (Croatia)|Prva ŽNL]], the fifth football level in Croatia. The greatest club success was in the 2002–03 season when they finished runners-up in the [[Croatian Football Cup|Croatian Cup]], losing to [[HNK Hajduk Split|Hajduk Split]] 5–0 on [[aggregate score|aggregate]]. In the 2004–05 season, the club changed its name into NK Pula 1856, because 1856 was the year that the [[Austro-Hungarian Empire]] made Pula the port of its arsenal and the shipyard [[Uljanik]] was opened. Also in the same year, it competed in the Prva HNL for the first time. In 2005, it was renamed again to NK Pula Staro Češko due to a sponsorship contract with the brewery Daruvarska pivovara (Staro Češko is a beer brand). Just one year later, the name was once again changed, this time to NK Pula. Again, just a year later in the middle of 2007, the name was changed for the fifth time in as many years, to NK Istra 1961. The change of name came after an ultimatum from the local fans Demoni who said the club would have their support only if the club changed its name and club colours to the traditional city colours (yellow and green). After renaming club was sold in 2011 to a Russian who achieved promotion for the club and sold it in 2015. Istra 1961{{Cite web|url=http://nkistrafan.weebly.com/about.html|title=About|website=nkistrafan.weebly.com|access-date=17 April 2017}} was bought by an American investment group in 2015. The Istra 1961's academy system consistently competes for top spots in the rankings. Istra 1961 has a rich fan history. The group of die hard fans are referred to as the Demoni, and are known for their explosive chants and celebrations as well as their extreme pride for the club. In summer 2018, club's ownership changed once again, this time to [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] consortium Baskonia - Alavés Group which acquired the majority share package and became sole owner of Istra 1961.{{cite web|title=Grupacija koja je podignula NK Rudeš preuzela Istru 1961: Slijede bolji dani za Istrijane! |trans-title=The group that raised NK Rudeš took over Istria in 1961: Better days for Istrians are coming!|url=https://gol.dnevnik.hr/clanak/rubrika/nogomet/grupacija-baskonia-alaves-iz-spanjolske-preuzela-nk-istru-1961---522071.html |publisher=Gol.hr |date=28 June 2018 |language=hr |access-date=22 December 2020}} Its crest features the city's [[Pula Arena|Roman arena in Pula]], as well as the old team crest. Istra 1961 play their home matches at the recently renovated [[Stadion Aldo Drosina]], which has a capacity of approximately 10,000 spectators."}}
